The **Persian Gulf**,[[a]]sometimes called the **Arabian Gulf**,[[b]] is a [mediterranean sea] in [West Asia]. The [body of water] is an extension of the [Arabian Sea] and the larger [Indian Ocean] located between the [Arabian Peninsula] and [Iran] (Persia).[[1]][[2]] It is connected to the [Gulf of Oman] in the east by the [Strait of Hormuz]. The [river delta] of the [Shatt al-Arab] forms the north-west shoreline.

The Persian Gulf has many fishing grounds, extensive [reefs] (mostly rocky, but also [coral]), and abundant [pearl oysters]; however, its [ecology] has been damaged by industrialization and [oil spills].

The Persian Gulf is in the [Persian Gulf Basin], which is of [Cenozoic] origin and related to the [subduction] of the [Arabian plate] under the [Zagros Mountains].[[3]] The current [flooding of the basin] started 15,000 years ago due to [rising sea levels] of the [Holocene glacial retreat].[[4]]

## Geography

See also: [Southern Iran], [Eastern Arabia], and [Arab states of the Persian Gulf]

The [International Hydrographic Organization] defines the Persian Gulf's southern limit as "The Northwestern limit of Gulf of Oman". This limit is defined as "A line joining Ràs Limah (25°57'N) on the coast of [Arabia] and Ràs al Kuh (25°48'N) on the coast of Iran ([Persia] "Fars (territory)"))".[[5]]%22%3Epage needed%3C/span%3E]]%3C/i%3E]%3C/sup%3E-7)

This inland sea of some 251,000 square kilometres (96,912 sq mi) is connected to the [Gulf of Oman] in the east by the [Strait of Hormuz]. Its western end is marked by the major [river delta] of the [Shatt al-Arab], which carries the waters of the [Euphrates] and the [Tigris]. In [Iran], this is called "Arvand Rud" (lit.'Swift River').

Its length is 989 kilometres (615 miles), with Iran covering most of the northern coast and [Saudi Arabia] most of the southern coast. The Persian Gulf is about 56 km (35 mi) wide at its narrowest, in the Strait of Hormuz. The waters are very shallow, with a maximum depth of 90 metres (295 feet) and an average depth of 50 metres (164 feet).

Countries with a coastline on the Persian Gulf are (clockwise, from north): Iran; [Oman]'s [Musandam exclave]; the [United Arab Emirates]; Saudi Arabia; [Qatar], on a [peninsula] off the Saudi coast; [Bahrain], an island nation; [Kuwait]; and [Iraq] in the northwest.
